text:
nina.arch: Quick thread — thinking about local attestation fallback for airgapped upgrades. RFC leans on controlplane attestations and audit logs, but offline sites will need a way to make deterministic allow/deny decisions with limited state. How do we design a minimal contract that keeps UX simple?

ben.ops: We should aim for a single compact token the operator can verify: signed manifest + expiry + policy-allow-bitmask. No heavy policy eval locally.

eli.runtime: Agree. Implementation note: signers rotate, so operator needs a small keyring and a way to accept an "escrowed" recovery key for emergency restores. But we must avoid prompting users for manual key import often.

zoe.sre: Resource note: some airgapped appliances only have 1 vCPU and 1GB RAM. Any crypto ops should be bounded and async during admin-initiated upgrade only. No background polling or heavy CRL checks.

nina.arch: Proposal sketch: 1) compact attestation envelope (CAE) containing: bundle-id, version, signer-id, policy-hash, allow-mask, expiry-epoch, optional-escrow-key-id. 2) operator validates signature, checks expiry, verifies bundle integrity via local hash, and then enforces allow-mask. 3) Control plane stores full audit and policy eval for later reconciliation when connected.

eli.runtime: Example CAE (inline):```json
{"v":"1","bundle":"bundle-2026-09-01","ver":"3","signer":"key-2026-06","policy_hash":"sha256:aa..","allow_mask":5,"exp":1735700000}
```

ben.ops: Want to call out allow_mask bits mapping: 1=install, 2=activate, 4=rollback. That keeps operator logic trivial (bitwise &).

zoe.sre: How do we treat expired CAEs? If operator is strictly offline for many months, expiry might block legitimate restores. Need a configurable grace window with owner confirmation. Also clock skew.

nina.arch: Right. Suggest operator supports three modes: enforce, grace-confirm, accept-old. Default for new installs = enforce. For upgrades from older versions default = grace-confirm which requires operator admin to run `operator upgrade-accept --approve-old` logging an explicit audit event locally.

eli.runtime: For escrow keys: we can support a short-lived one-time recovery token embedded in signed CAE that operator can import with `operator import-escrow --token <token>`; token itself is signed and includes operator-id + expiry. Avoid keeping long-lived escape keys on device.

ben.ops: Telemetry policy: in grace-confirm mode we must not auto-upload anything. When connectivity resumes, operator pushes a reconciliation packet with local audit log. Customer must opt-in to automatic uploads.

zoe.sre: Testing: add scenarios: extreme clock skew (+/- 48h), operator with wiped /etc/keys, long offline (180 days), interrupted activation mid-apply. Also measure verification latency on 1 vCPU/1GB.

nina.arch: UX: operator CLI should be a three line interactive flow for permissive accept: show bundle summary, show policy_hash and signer, require typed confirmation string, create local audit record. No hidden defaults.

eli.runtime: We should publish a small reference library in Rust and Go ~<30KB binary when stripped, no deps beyond ring or go/crypto, to make it easy for integrators to reuse. Keep verification deterministic and avoid network calls.

ben.ops: Migration path: for existing installs, operator upgrade will add keyring and a "bootstrap-escrow" flow. We'll provide a one-time signed provisioning artifact that contains organization key metadata for migration.

zoe.sre: Ops playbook: emergency rollback requires operator admin + offline confirmation token; add step to collect local audit bundle and upload during incident reconciliation.

deploy-bot: New RFC draft: https://git.redwood.internal/rfcs/offline-compact-attestation. Commit by nina.arch.

nina.arch: Thanks all. Action items: eli to prototype CAE parser + verifier (PoC binary), ben to write operator CLI flow, zoe to add test matrices, I'll draft RFC appendix with allow_mask and migration steps. Sync Monday 9am PT.
